reviews.title: Inaccurate
reviews.text: This app is truly the worst food tracker I have ever used. They have a lot of gimmicky AI features, but it cannot accurately capture the nutrition facts even of common, commercially available packaged products. This app added a lot of stress to my life and I just had to stop using it

reviews.title: AI slop
reviews.text:
I was excited to sign up and get my appointment, which was easy to do. But the amount of AI is just, well, not for me at all. This app should be called Nourish AI because that’s all it is really. 

Deleted my account as there are better food logging apps out there.

reviews.title: LEAVE THE APP ALONE
reviews.text: For the love of GOD ALMIGHTY please stop changing the app, it went from intuitive, data-driven, quick and painless to the worst app I’ve ever used with EVERY NEW UPDATE. Also it’s just not necessary to change it so frequently. Seriously developers leave it alone, in fact revert it to 5 versions ago. I hate using it so much, I no longer record my meals on the app which means I have to find alternative ways to get that information to my dietitian—which means more work for both of us. I’m two seconds away from rejoining MyNetDiary and using that as my food log because I don’t want to have to re-learn this app every week. Please stop, please, I’m begging you.

reviews.title: Just stop please
reviews.text: Please stop altering this app.  The changes are too frequent and nothing actually improves.  It’s just a continuous learning curve and discourages the user.

reviews.title: Good but lacking cgm or wearable integrationd
reviews.text: The good : Ai chat and ai food recognition. Messaging with your dietitian. Pulls some data from apple health. The bad : Not able to sync with apple health to get your excersise data , no sync with cgm like lingo to get your glucose data.

reviews.title: Service is great, app isn’t
reviews.text: The service provided is great, the app could use some work

reviews.title: Nourish app use
reviews.text: This is the absolute worst app I’ve ever use. The date does not update, the list of foods with their proteins , carbs etc does not update to the correct amounts , it place lunches where dinners should be. I keep writing the email help for the company but while they offer the same recover and over again … the recommendations are the same over and over again . They should look to the Weight Watcher app to improve theirs . I’m tired of writing for help.

reviews.title: Getting worse every release
reviews.text: Whoever keeps trying to jam AI into the app every which way, and keeps messing up logging food, needs to step away from the keyboard. The logging flow keeps getting more convoluted and introducing mistakes (I choose one recent meal, it logs a different one. I scan a bar code, it correctly identifies it but logs very incorrect data for it. etc. etc. ) If I can’t trust the logging, it will quickly become useless.

reviews.title: New Update Ruined App experience
reviews.text: The 10/1 update ruined the app for me. No info given at all when tracking. Can no longer scan my food or barcodes. No nutritional info for any meals so what’s the point of tracking?? Only reason I even entertain tracking is for my coach to see what I eat. Going to just use my Cal AI app that actually tracks calories/ protein/fiber, relevant info I need to actually stay on track with the goals my nutritional coach and I discussed. Would rather take screenshots from that app and send to my coach than use the Nourish app.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Never knew my insurance paid for a nutritionist and blood work all in one app. It’s clever with logging your meals with a picture. Getting instant AI feedback. Impressive my first week so far.

reviews.title: Tracker needs improvements
reviews.text: I am fortunate to have this service and enjoyed my first counseling session but tracking the food on this app is awful. I select dinner and it puts the food as breakfast. I track a snack and it adds it to dinner. I tracked black coffee and it showed with hundreds of calories. I can’t figure out how to track for the previous day. Perhaps a tutorial would help.

reviews.title: You didn’t fix what we asked
reviews.text:
I still cannot type in special movements under “Other“, you promised to fix this with this update and you failed

Every update you put out is a testament to doing everything against what your users have ask you to do.

Every update makes this app more and more difficult to personalize my usage of it. It is now completely taken over by AI. We don’t want AI. We want to write it in ourselves. This app is getting worse and worse every time.

The only reason I stick around is because of my nutritionist and she actually agrees with me, but but then again you don’t do what your employees ask you to do, either.

reviews.title: Good but needs some improvements
reviews.text: The overall Nourish experience with the app and dietitian has been good.  I feel it’s very personalized.  I like that they are certified dietitians and my insurance covers it 100 percent. With that being said. The 1 star I took off is for the app.  It has a lot of items that are not correct in the database.  So I always have to double check the labels which can become time consuming. If it was once in a while I’d understand but it happens a lot. The other star is that I had to reach out  to billing because after 4 weeks they started charging a co pay. I reach out to my insurance and Nourish had started billing incorrectly. After 4 weeks hmmm Just be mindful and keep an eye on the nutrition info on the items and billing if you notice a change.  It is definitely worth looking into.

reviews.title: Add Apple Health active calorie import
reviews.text: I wish it automatically pulled my active calories burned from Apple Health to show me how many calories extra I need to eat to hit a deficit. Switched to Cronometer Gold because Nourish doesn’t have that.

reviews.title: Awesome 💕
reviews.text:
I found out about Nourish from an ad on Facebook, and I was immediately interested because it said the service could be covered by insurance. I decided to take a chance and enter my information—and to my surprise, it’s 100% covered! I was so excited! 🥹❤️

I’m currently 5’1” and around 350 pounds. I’ve been wanting to lose weight for a while, but one of my biggest struggles has been finding the motivation to stay consistent. I’m really hoping Nourish can help me stay accountable and finally make lasting changes.

I have a 1-year-old son, and one of my biggest motivations is being able to do more with him. Right now, my weight limits me in ways that I don’t want it to. I want to be healthier, have more energy, and be able to enjoy life and make memories with my family without feeling so limited.

I recently had my first appointment with my dietitian, and it went really well! I genuinely really like her. She was so kind, friendly, and actually took the time to listen to me. I don’t have many friends in real life, so honestly, talking to her felt like talking to a friend. 🥹

I’m so excited to officially begin this healthy journey with Nourish. This time, I have access to a nutrition professional who can help guide me, keep me accountable, and teach me how to make healthier choices that I can actually maintain.

I’m hoping that having this support will make a difference in my results this time around.

Here’s to becoming healthier, stronger, and more active for myself and my family. ❤️

I’ll update you all in 6 months! 🥰

reviews.title: App can’t add
reviews.text: Enter a meal, use the same meal the next day with a few changes, the app forgets how to add and blows up the macro counts

reviews.title: New update is ugly and clumsy
reviews.text:
Please go back to the old app. You made it more difficult to use. I didn’t think it could get worse after the last makeover several months ago, but you did it. This is way worse. Used this app for over a year, love my dietician, but I can’t track if it takes twice as long.

UPDATE 10/1/26: app won’t log food correctly, makes up its own numbers when specifically given macros. Still clumsy and annoying

reviews.title: Log meal
reviews.text: Logging meals is clunky. I’ve used other apps that are much easier

reviews.title: The app does not work
reviews.text: Sure you can download the app, but it never loads anything and doesn’t keep you signed in. You have to go to a web browser to do anything at all. And you have to log in every. Single. Time.

reviews.title: Great dietitians ruined by forced AI
reviews.text: I've been using this app for about 2 years. I've witnessed it go from a decent food log to an AI chat bot sloplog. I absolutely hate using this app from their having to prompt every food picture you input to their forced AI meal suggestions. This app forces so much AI on you without giving you the option to turn out off. I've emailed support regarding this issue and my initial email was responded by an AI where when i then wanted to speak to a human was greeted with AI responses basically telling me i cant turn certain features off. The funny part was a year ago the response when I emailed support it was actually person rather than an AI response. When I meet with my dietitian their view of my log looks great and the mobile app was close to it where it was just a food log not a chat room.   I don’t mind some of the AI features like you used to be able to take a picture of your food it will then use AI to decipher the items and measurements and then if the log was wrong you can then re-prompt it to the correct values but now they don’t even give you that option It’s like you’re messaging a bot that messages back meal suggestions that I don’t own the ingredients for. The only good thing about this app is my dietition who I talked to on zoom

reviews.title: AI needs to be cleaned up
reviews.text:
The RD part of nourish is unparalleled. Experts who support good eating habits and back it up with science. 

The AI part of logging food is cumbersome, and makes a simple task one that I dislike doing everyday. 

Please make logging food more intuitive - if I logged an item - make that item also visible. It’s nested in a meal and hard to find. Let me favorite items I’ve logged to make it easier to find. 

I don’t ALWAYS eat the same thing day in a day out. Thank you!

reviews.title: New interface is awful
reviews.text: I used Nourish consistently for months and now it is too much effort to log a meal.  Talk about overkill with all the AI clutter!!

reviews.title: Less AI more UI/UX designer
reviews.text: Stop overloading this app with ai slop. Hire really good designers and get back to the basics. You won’t get more customers by adding more unnecessary features. Focus on how to make logging easier and more straightforward.

reviews.title: Horrid design
reviews.text: This app is way too busy. The process of logging is so frustrating that it makes me want to stop the program all together. The barcode scanning is hardly accurate and I have edit almost every single time I use it. Please find a way to simplify/streamline things.

reviews.title: App is unusable
reviews.text: I used to be able to use an app of my choosing. Then they took that away. And now the required app has been redesigned by someone apparently unfamiliar with both apps in general and the actual user tasks in particular. Fortunately, it often simply doesn’t work, so it’s usually broken instead of stupid.

reviews.title: AI model needs upgraded + some logging locked behind goals
reviews.text: The AI model that this app uses  is not particularly precise or accurate. For example, I might take a picture of a nutrition label and say “log 2 servings” and it logs 1 serving or it only applies the 2x multiplier to one of the fields instead of all. Sometimes it misses certain data fields altogether (for example, it forgot to include added sugars for a slice of cake). Sometimes it arrives at completely different values for the exact same meal. It would be great if a more recent or higher tier model was used instead. Additionally, the interface seems to lock certain data tracking behind “goals”, but there is an arbitrary limit of 5 goals, so I’m not able to log everything that I would like to log in the app.

reviews.title: Would be better if they stopped doing updates
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app on and off for almost a year now. I find it incredibly frustrating how often they update the app to better it. The new AI update drives me nuts, I want to be able to disable all of the AI functionality like it giving me prompts for questions about eating habits. I’m not anti-AI by any means, but I don’t like how it feels like I have a chat bot now and the logging and everything else comes separately. Let me toggle on and off the tabs at the bottom of the UX.

reviews.title: Incorrect log information
reviews.text: I’ve been using the app since February and while the app is so helpful, I’ve noticed that the app calculates the food intake values incorrectly. For example, the app is saying I have almost 4,000mg of sodium for my intake yesterday and I only had about half of that. This concerns me for all of my logs since I started using the app.

reviews.title: Crashes
reviews.text:
Can’t really do much with the latest update as it crashes after the app has been open for about 5-10sec. Making essentially worthless. 

Was useful previously.

reviews.title: No Messaging
reviews.text: I can’t message anyone because there is a giant blue box telling me about a possible $75 fee I may incur. The blue box covers everything and won’t go away. This makes the app almost useless.

reviews.title: Why?
reviews.text: The app was fine. It was updated and not it’s terrible to navigate. I hate the new update!

reviews.title: New update
reviews.text: I’ve used the nourish app for about 8 months now and it always had some issues but was starting to get better, then the most recent update has been very difficult to navigate and the most frustrating thing is the inaccuracies in tracking. It does not track macros accurately on the first attempt and when trying to switch between different measurements it has very inaccurate calculations. I hope the bugs are fixed soon and the app becomes easier to use again.

reviews.title: Latest SW update slows it down
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app since Jan 2026 and I’ve loved it. I’ve lost 30 lbs so far. Tracking food was easy, scheduling my nutritionist and communicating with him through the app is good. BUT, the latest SW update has slooowed down logging in food. It’s. It my internet connection since o have a strong connection at my home and nothing’s changed there. And I feel like I have to do an extra step to get my food logged in. Also, the placement of some of the entries are too far to the edge and hard to click on (in the mobile version).

reviews.title: Not user friendly
reviews.text: Good information given after logging food, but the app isn’t user friendly when logging a meal. Not easy to navigate either

reviews.title: Not Functional At All
reviews.text: I have attempted to log weight, meals, etc. and none of it works. I don’t even have a home button. Even if you can meet with a dietician what is the point if you can’t use anything on the app? Not to mention my experience with my dietician was not great. 15-20 minutes late with no explanation, no set goals, eating on the call. Not impressed.

reviews.title: Good app but latest update is awful
reviews.text: You can’t edit entries if you need to change something, you have to delete and reenter everything. Too heavily relies on AI. It does now include added sugar which is nice. Would really prefer to not to use this app but my nutritionist is awesome and the only truly good thing about this app.

reviews.title: Bring the old version back
reviews.text: The recent update is just frustrating and annoying. I do not want to have a conversation with AI whenever i log my food. I just need an app that connects me to my nutritionist, log my food, calculates calories and nutrients. Tried the new version twice and it’s just a waste of my time. Will not be using anymore.

reviews.title: Dishonest Advertising
reviews.text:
I scheduled a basic lab panel through Nourish for today, and when I showed up the Quest Diagnostics employee could not find my order.  It turns out Nourish had listed my nickname on the lab order and not my legal first name (which they have on file with my insurance).  I cancelled the lab, edited my information in the app, and tried to re-schedule the lab.

When I tried rescheduling, the app would no longer let me edit the appointment and said that the test would now cost me $19.  The AI support bot on the phone told me about some update to charges in July (which I can find no information about), and when I was finally forwarded to a human representative he said something about an update that happened when I was in the middle of scheduling.  It was sketchy and vague.

The app and website advertise a free basic panel for patients once every three months.  Today proved that they do not honor this advertised service.  I have contacted customer service again via email and got an AI-generated response that they were escalating the issue to a team member.  I will update my review if any improvement is made.

My nutritionist, Laura, is the only redeeming quality that this company has.  She’s amazing.

reviews.title: Meal logging is a mess
reviews.text: The app has no easy way to return to yesterdays meals even when it says you are logging for yesterday, it logs it on today’s date. Annoying.

reviews.title: App change sucks
reviews.text: This used to be a really easy app to use. They have made recent updates that make it incredibly frustrating on their main page. It tries to do too much and you accidentally click buttons. It’s definitely not user-friendly. If you can find a different app, I would suggest you go that route.

reviews.title: Scrolling feed is too confusing
reviews.text: The new layout of the app is very confusing. I can never tell where one day ends and the next one begins. If I need to scroll back a few days, I have to scroll and scroll instead of being able to go up to the top and switch days like it used to do. The need to double click an entry because it acts like it is a “post” on the app is very annoying. The number of times I thought I had posted a meal only to realize I had forgotten to click the second time….  I will say the food search has improved. I don’t particularly like the AI picture system.

reviews.title: New Update makes it tough
reviews.text: I first got this app and loved that I was able to edit and add whenever I wanted. This new update has made uploading this one very long AI text conversation which is not very friendly to enter updates. It’s almost impossible now to find the message center to chat with your dietician. It also got rid of every piece of color it had to differentiate between protein and fiber intake. The interface was much better before. I love improving things but this makes it almost unbearable to use right now

reviews.title: UI isn’t good and hard to add stuff without it making mistakes.
reviews.text: There are better apps out there

reviews.title: STOP CHANGING IT
reviews.text: They change this app every week or two, and each update makes the app less and less user friendly.  I am honestly considering deleting and quitting Nourish out of sheer frustration that every time I get used to one app change, they do another, and somehow all of the changes make it more difficult to (1) log food and (2) message your nutritionist, which are kind of the two most important things.  If you want to improve functionality, great, but please, for the love of God, STOP CHANGING THE INTERFACE!

reviews.title: Change app back to normal
reviews.text: I don’t like new app

reviews.title: New AI update is awful
reviews.text: The app was so easy to use before this update. It’s so hard to log meals now if you scan a label, the nutrition facts are almost never accurate before the update they almost always were. The dietitian support is still great, but the app itself needs a lot of improvements after the last update.

reviews.title: App is getting worse every update
reviews.text: Aside from bug fixes that did help, all other major changes are steps in the wrong direction. It feels like the design team is experimenting with very different UI options. The app right now has a 100% different interface to log meals than it had a year ago and it is super confusing and difficult to use. Can’t answer a simple question such as what is my daily nutrition trend over past X days. Who mocks with something that used to work and makes it consistently worse with each update? I am thinking of quitting the whole service because how useless the app is and I do like my personal nutritionist a lot, but this is not working at all!

reviews.title: Great until recent updates
reviews.text: Nourish has always utilized AI in its app, but the recent updates are pushing your interaction with that part of the app. The updates are not intuitive and make logging clunky. I had months-long streaks prior to these updates, and now I dread logging. The AI also (poorly) summarized a note I’d made in a way that my dietitian could only read the summary and not what I’d actually written. I loved this app before, and now I’m finding myself contemplating discontinuing use. I do love my dietitian though, so it’s a hard choice.

reviews.title: I hate the new interface
reviews.text: I love my dietitian, but I hate all the AI and the interface catered to the chat bot model. It’s too chaotic and it’s turning me off, honestly. I might have to leave this platform altogether. I already don’t care for logging meals, but this new interface has made me dislike it even more.

reviews.title: Excellent app best I’ve ever used
reviews.text: App is amazing. I thought I would continue to use my fitness pal for food tracking, but this gives me everything. I need to check my macros exercise and hydration. The AI suggestions for next meal recommendations to hit my macros are great. using the app is a lot of fun

reviews.title: App upgrade with AI makes me track less
reviews.text: This new app update rolled out AI tracking.  If I want to do manual, it’s cluttered and hard to navigate, so I don’t track much anymore.  The AI is hard to use to get the macros right and its suggestions are often not what you intend.

reviews.title: It’s not just the App that’s frustrating
reviews.text: I just recently joined and the website is just as frustrating.  Confusing menu, “features” are not user friendly to understand immediately and duplicating data entries from another day or time, is  a mess. Just to name a few. “Add free form“?  How about just “Manual entry.”  Simple.  They should hire some software testers before they make updates and make substantial changes to the user  interface

reviews.title: Archaic and Frustrating Approaches
reviews.text: In three months, I went through three different dietitians. They each have no idea how to treat metabolic syndrome such as PMOS/PCOS. They tell you to eat more often and eat more carbs and have no idea about blood sugar management and the metabolic intricacies of a condition. In the three months I gained weight my PCOS/PMOS symptoms got worse and I decided to fully delete the app and deactivate my account and go back to what I was doing because I was able to manage my metabolic syndrome better than 3 registered dieticians. Do not waste your time.

reviews.title: Get rid of AI
reviews.text: I don’t like using AI. I don’t like watching the screen recalibrate. I want simple. Less stuff on the screen. I need to be able to see my numbers and if I want to look back I have scroll so far. Please simplify.

reviews.title: App update
reviews.text: Really missing the old app. This new version is not as nice a the old one.

reviews.title: Weight log
reviews.text: The weight log doesn’t let adjust your weight goal or see a true progress.  Not user friendly. The rest of the app is great.

reviews.title: Bring the last version back!!
reviews.text: I’ve been using the nourish app since late December and I think this is the 2nd update that has changed the look, feel and usability.  The last version was, in my opinion, the best.  It wasn’t perfect but once I got used to it was really helpful for my health journey.  I’ve experienced numerous issues with the current version, and I might add the look and functionality is super clunky and difficult.   Some of my issues: favorites and recent foods not saved/visible, meals added that I didn’t enter, meals duplicated over inflating my scores, photos of food not loading.  Please seriously review this app update.  If the tool isn’t user friendly people won’t use it and the information (accurate information) is critical for the visit with the nutritionist.  Thanks!

reviews.title: Update not user friendly
reviews.text: Loved the previous version, absolutely hate the updated interface. Please consider returning to the previous version and make sure the AI tool is accurate.

reviews.title: Updates Suck
reviews.text: Used to love this app but now tracking meals is impossibly hard!

reviews.title: Great dietitian, terrible app
reviews.text:
I recently started using Nourish and absolutely love my dietitian—she has helped me achieve great results. However, the app itself is extremely frustrating. The calorie calculations are often incorrect, even when I scan the nutrition label and enter the correct grams, making food tracking take twice as long as it did with MyFitnessPal.

I also don’t like how meals are organized. I should be able to click on “Lunch” or “Dinner” and immediately see my total protein, calories, etc., instead of manually adding everything together. Tracking food is already difficult, and the app makes it unnecessarily complicated. At this point, I’m considering going back to MyFitnessPal and simply sharing my food logs with my dietitian.

reviews.title: Great service, sick of AI
reviews.text: I’ve had great success finding a dietitian & have been working with them for over a year now. It has been an overall wonderful experience that I would highly recommend to anyone looking for ways to improve their health & relationship with food. However, recently, the app has been shifting towards an AI-focused approach with the home page literally being an AI chat interface. In addition to this, I am shown daily AI suggestions (which are sometimes triggering & counter-productive to my goals), autofilled AI prompts are constantly positioned at the bottoms of all tabs, & the AI is also not providing accurate information, for something as simple as “where do I find this hand-out” bc everything has been moved around & are far less intuitive. I will continue using Nourish, as it has been an incredible tool & service in my health journey, but I have found myself using the app itself less & less, and I am disappointed at the AI-centric direction it has gone.

reviews.title: New UI is frustrating
reviews.text: The newest UI is a real bummer. I loved tracking in Nourish before.  Were there a few tweaks I wished for, yes… but overall it was a positive experience.  With the new UI, the rolling log of the day is not helpful, it’s confusing because you see a summary of your day’s progress from various parts of the day. Then there is another tab that has similar info but different, but not different in a helpful way. I am struggling to easily find the foods I’ve previously had (that weren’t from a super recent meal). I used to log religiously and now find myself not logging for parts of my day since it takes more time and is not an enjoyable experience. I hope the engineering team has some folks reviewing this user experience and is logging needed fixes for an upcoming sprint release.

reviews.title: New update is not user friendly
reviews.text: I’ve been using the Nourish app for almost a year and the latest UI is not user friendly. It’s impossible to figure out which days you’re tracking. It is very confusing and hard to see or add meals. Please revert to a calendar view.

reviews.title: Pushing GLP1s
reviews.text: This app pushes GLP1s. I’m 5’5 and 148 lbs. I do not need a GLP1! I swiped twice and it still continues to come up in the app. I just wanted to learn how to eat better. It’s not really helpful to me. So I deleted it.

reviews.title: Update is awful!
reviews.text: I’ve used the Nourish app for over a year, but took a brief break this summer. I came back this morning to the most useless update—why have you changed things that worked?? I don’t want an AI summary, I just want to log my meals. I don’t want AI to give me suggestions, I just want to check my protein and fiber intake and stay on track nutritionally. Make it fun, make it a game, but please do not make it frustrating. I’m so disappointed…

reviews.title: Used to be great
reviews.text: Im completely frustrated with this app after the new update that was done a couple of weeks ago. The AI feature is a little less accurate than it was before the update. I will describe the meal with ounces and cup size and it is given ridiculous amount of calories. Then I remove items and it increases the number of calories. Also the colors were better before the update. What happened? Bring back the old version!!

reviews.title: Difficulty deleting data
reviews.text: The app has some interesting features however somehow one of my meals keeps getting logged in and is now showing up 4 times.  I have not figured out how delete the errant entries.  I do mot find the program to be very intuitive to use.

reviews.title: Surprise Charge
reviews.text: I just received an email requesting an updated payment method for an appointment I had back in April, which I was told would be covered by insurance. I got an email in May that my insurance would not cover any future appointments, and that I could opt to have any prior non-covered charges dismissed before selecting self-pay, which I did. Now, Nourish is trying to charge me for an appointment that occurred well before this notification and claiming I selected self-pay, which is kit the case because I never even had a payment method on file to begin with!

reviews.title: Horrible customer service
reviews.text: Love my nutritionist the customer support is horrible. Automated copy and paste replies to every message and zero accountability or transparency around price changes.

reviews.title: Too much Ai
reviews.text: The Update is horrible. I liked the older version. It’s so hard to see your progress. It relies too heavily on Ai and it’s annoying

reviews.title: Frustrating
reviews.text:
I only recently started using this, and I found it impressive, until a recent change that made the user interface harder. Another issue that’s come up is that the AI no longer seems to understand that if I post a recipe and then tell it I ate half, it still logs it as if I ate the entire dang skillet. The ability to edit it afterwards is also diminished. 
The thing I liked was how much work the AI did for me and now I find myself back to doing a lot of work again. Time to roll back the change.

reviews.title: Please stop the updates
reviews.text: This last update made me come and post a review, I used to love the app and the latest update was too much. It’s nothing like it was before. Why have there been so many updates and changes in the last several weeks? Now it’s almost fully ai based and a ghost of an app that it was before.

reviews.title: Better apps exist
reviews.text: New design is terrible. I already didn’t find the app that great for logging food. Over reliance on AI means a lot of common meals from restaurants aren’t even easily findable. The AI will estimate something crazy off and then recalculate to something totally different. Other apps for logging have been so much better for me. I’ve almost given up trying to log foods on the app

reviews.title: AI Slop Once Again
reviews.text: I love my nutritionist so far & we have really worked on a great plan to get me to my goals but it is IMPOSSIBLE to log anything into this app. I don't want AI guessing how many calories are in a meal it cannot weigh correctly, it even gets barcoded items incorrect. It told me a packet of noodles at least 50cal under what the label said. I don't like that. I especially don't like when the only option to log my calories is to either use the AI or nothing at all. Let me input the weight & measurements of what i'm eating so i can log my progress manually, PLEASE! reviews.title: The new update ruined the app
reviews.text:
I really liked Nourish for the 50 days I used it. I liked my dietitian, I liked the app, and I had gotten into a good routine with logging my meals. Unfortunately, the latest app update completely changed that experience for me.

The new layout is unnecessarily complicated, and what used to be a simple process of searching for and logging food now feels like a chore. I am perfectly capable of searching the food database or scanning a barcode. I don’t need AI involved in every step of logging my food.

The most frustrating part is that I had spent the last month and a half building up meals and snacks that I regularly eat and correcting the nutritional information when the AI got it wrong. My meals are no longer searchable when I go to log a new meal. So even though I have already done the work, I can’t easily reuse those entries like I use to be able to.

I contacted support about the issue, and this is where things became even more frustrating. Nourish states that it uses “Nourish’s AI assistant to help resolve your question as quickly as possible.” Based on the responses I received, I honestly don’t know whether an actual person ever reviewed my original message. I had to clarify multiple times to the AI assistant that my meals were NOT missing from my history. They were still there. The problem was specifically that my previously saved and corrected meals were no longer searchable when I went to log a meal that I have had in the past. The initial responses completely missed that distinction and gave me troubleshooting steps for a problem I wasn’t having and I had to write a new email since AI misunderstood me.

I understand that someone put a lot of work into designing the new app, but this update feels like a classic case of trying to reinvent the wheel when the wheel was already working just fine.

I actually liked this app before the update. That’s what makes this so disappointing. I ultimately deleted the app because using it had become so frustrating, and I really hope Nourish reconsiders some of these changes. I would love to be able to recommend it again, but right now I can’t.

First off, now I HAVE to use AI to do anything. I tried logging my symptoms, but I can’t keep the log in my own words anymore. Instead, AI makes a summary. Third, it is now more confusing to just view my log. The AI is always interrupting in some way.  Don’t get me wrong, there was AI in the previous version. However, it was much less involved and I didn’t have to go through it all the time. 

The create recipe function needs to be fixed. I try to upload a recipe, but then the AI just makes its own…like no, that’s not what I made?? 


Something I wish they had is a way to break down the type of fat and fiber in the foods I am eating. This shouldn’t be too difficult for the app to do. It’s really important for people trying to track how much saturated fat they are having. For fiber, I’m supposed to have a higher ratio of soluble fiber. If I could see on my app how much soluble fiber i’ve had, it would make it so much easier than having to google everything and keep track separately. 

Anyway my dietician rocks. I love her, but the app is nearly impossible and I hate using it!

Not long after my initial consultation, the app transitioned to an AI driven platform that is HORRIBLE. Even when you take a picture of the label, the AI WILL make errors, forcing me to correct those errors for correct logging. reviews.title: Way too much AI

TLDR: way too much reliance on AI that doesn’t work very well.
I wanted to like this service so much, but I really hated the app. I have a Fitbit, but the app wouldn’t let me connect it to track my exercise, so I had to log all that manually. Plus the AI food logging is supposed to be convenient, but I had to edit just about every single entry I made because the AI got it wrong, even if I told it the specific brand & serving size I was eating. And then it would give feed back on each individual meal without taking into account what else I had eaten that day. For example, I had a rice cake with peanut butter and example as an afternoon snack, and the AI suggested “add more protein next time”, but I was already nearly at my protein goal for the whole day and hadn’t even eaten dinner yet! 

I did like the meal planning function that my dietician ran and provided to me each week, although some of those recipes and portioning were clearly AI influenced. Like it suggested as a snack 2 whole apples and 4 1/2 tbsp of peanut butter 😂
I’m sure it was to get me to my calorie goal for the day, but I think it would make more sense to add some more calories into lunch or dinner.

reviews.title: Update is way worse
reviews.text:
I usually don’t write bad reviews. If something bothers me or I don’t like it, I just stop using it or send it back, but I wanted to give my honest opinion on here about my disappointment in the new app updates. If nothing else, I hope that if the app developers are committed to user feedback they will take the time to read actual customers reviews and adjust accordingly. In the last 6 months or so, it seems that the app has undergone two major updates that have progressively made the app harder to use, more confusing, and less “user friendly.” 
We are all busy. The last thing we want to do multiple times a day is have to open an app at every mealtime and clumsily navigate through a set of unclear (and small) buttons just to track our macros. We want simple, clear, and easy instructions right on the home page. We want to open it up and see where we are at for the day and how we are doing. We want to be able to open the app and snap a picture as easily as we can without having to click through several pages or tabs to get there. The new, small buttons in the corner make it much harder to do this, and easier to accidentally click the wrong one. We don’t need the entire AI summary of every meal we have. Nobody cares about that. We want to open it and see very easily where we stand for the day and make decisions for ourselves about our next meal. If we want ideas or guidance, we should have a tab that we can navigate to on our own. Please consider going back to the previous versions where calories, hydration, and macro breakdowns were at the top of the home page clearly visible and easily accessible. It was easy to open the app and take a quick glance to see how many calories you had left for the day, and you could navigate seamlessly throughout each day prior. I enjoyed using the app then. Now I dread it. In my opinion, the new update is so unnecessary and full of useless information that I don’t want to read all day long. I am considering canceling my subscription altogether if this trend continues..
